chunks: 19 - In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. (3)

The shaykh, the jurist Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us by recitation upon him. He said: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Isa al-Yaqtini, from Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Farawi (4), from his father. He said:

I visited al-Fadl ibn al-Rabi' and he was sitting on a roof. He said to me: Come near to me. So I approached until I was alongside him. Then he said to me: Look toward the room in the house. So I looked, and he said: What do you see in the room? I said: A garment laid out. He said: Look carefully. So I pondered and looked and became certain. I said: A man in prostration. He said to me: Do you know him? I said: No. He said: This is your master. I said: And who is my master? He said: Are you feigning ignorance with me? I said: I am not feigning ignorance, but I do not know a master.

Then he said: This is Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him). Indeed I check on him day and night, and I have not found him at any time except in the state which I shall describe to you: He prays Fajr and then follows it with worship for an hour after his prayer until the sun rises. Then he prostrates and does not cease being in prostration until the sun passes midday. He had appointed someone to watch for the midday for him, and I do not know when the boy says: The sun has passed midday! — when he leaps up and begins the prayer without renewing his ablution, so I know that he did not sleep during his prostration nor did he drowse. He remains like that until he finishes the Asr prayer. When he prays Asr, he prostrates and does not cease being in prostration until the sun sets. When the sun sets, he leaps from his prostration and prays Maghrib without renewing anything. He remains in his prayer and worship until he prays the Isha prayer. When he prays Isha, he breaks his fast on something roasted (1) that is brought to him. Then he renews his ablution, then he prostrates, then he raises his head and sleeps a light nap. Then he rises and renews his ablution, then he rises and does not cease praying in the depths of the night until dawn rises. I do not know when the boy says: Indeed the dawn has risen! — when he has already leaped up for the Fajr prayer. This has been his habit since he was transferred to me. So I said: Fear God, and do not do anything regarding his affair that would cause the removal of blessings. For indeed you know that no one does harm to any one of them except that his blessings vanish.

He said: They have sent to me on more than one occasion commanding me to kill him, but I did not answer them to that, and I informed them that I would not do that, and even if they kill me I would not answer them to what they asked me. After that, he was transferred to al-Fadl ibn Yahya al-Barmaki, and he was imprisoned with him for days. Al-Fadl ibn al-Rabi' used to send him a meal every night, and it was forbidden for anyone else to enter upon him. So he would not eat and would not break his fast except on the meal that was brought to him, until three days and their nights passed in that condition. When it was the fourth night, a meal was presented to him from al-Fadl ibn Yahya. He said:

Then he (peace be upon him) raised his hand toward the sky and said: O Lord, indeed You know that if I had eaten before today, I would have aided against myself. He said: So he ate and fell ill. The next day, a doctor was sent to him to ask about the illness. The doctor said to him: What is your condition? He ignored him. When the doctor persisted, he showed him the palm of his hand, then said: This is my illness. And there was a greenness in the middle of his palm, indicating that it was poison that had gathered in that spot. He said: The doctor departed to them and said: By God, he knows what you did to him more than you do! Then he (peace be upon him) passed away. (1)

key_terms.العتمة: Al-Atama — refers to the Isha (night) prayer
key_terms.تعقيب: Ta'qib — post-prayer supplications and worship following the obligatory prayer
key_terms.زوال النعمة: Removal of blessings — a warning that harming the Ahl al-Bayt leads to loss of divine favor
key_terms.سم: Poison — the means by which the Imam was martyred
key_terms.مولاك: Your master/lord — referring to Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS), the seventh Imam

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Musa al-Kadhim worship during his imprisonment?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Amali of al-Shaykh al-Saduq describes the extraordinary worship of Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) during his imprisonment by the Abbasid caliph Harun al-Rashid. The narrator, Abdullah al-Farawi's father, visited the prison warden al-Fadl ibn al-Rabi', who showed him the Imam in a state of continuous prostration and prayer from dawn to dusk and through the night. Al-Fadl refused repeated orders to kill the Imam, but after the Imam was transferred to al-Fadl ibn Yahya al-Barmaki, he was poisoned through his food and martyred.

en.bilal-muhammad: Abu Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (ra) narrated to us. My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us from Muhammad b. `Isa al-Yaqtini from Ahmad b. `Abdullah al-Farwi from his father.

He said: I visited Fadl b. Rabih and he was sitting on the roof. He said: Come to me. I went close that I was right next to him. He said: Look to the side of that house. I looked to where he pointed, then he asked me: What do you see in the house? I said: I see a thrown cloak. He said: Look closer. I gazed attentively and scrutinized my vision, and then I was certain. I said: A man in prostration. He said: Do you know him? I said: No. He said: This is your master. I said: Who is my master? He said: Are you fooling me? I said: I am not fooling you. I do not know a master.

Then he said: This is Abu’l Ḥasan Musa b. Ja`far. I inspect him day and night, and I have not seen him at any time except in this state which I shall describe to you: He prays Fajr, and afterwards he follows that with worship for an hour after his prayer (ta`qib) till sunrise. He then bows down in a prostrates and remains in prostration till midday. Someone was appointed to him to check for midday; I do not know when the boy recognizes that the Sun has reached midday. Then, [the Imam] rises and begins his [Thuhr] prayer, without renewing his ritual ablutions (wudu’), and by this I know that he has not slept during his prostration and did not drowse. He remains in this state [of worship] till he finishes the `Asr prayer. If he prays `Asr, he then bows in a prostration and remains in prostration until the Sun sets. When the Sun sets, he rises from prostration and prays Maghrib without renewing anything, and he remains in the state of prayer and worship until he prays the first night prayer (`Isha’). When he finishes all this, he breaks his fast on something roasted that is brought to him. He then renews his ablutions. After that, he rises and spends the whole night in worship until dawn. I do not know how the boy recognizes and tells that it is time for Fajr, that I see him [Imam Musa] rising for Fajr prayer. This has been his state since the time he was transferred to me. Then, I said: Fear Allah, and do not do something ill to him which might cause you to be deprived of grace. You know well that no one does harm to one of them [the Ahl al-Bayt] without their bounties vanishing.

He said: They sent to me more than once commanding me to kill him but I did not answer them to this, and I made them know that I will not do this, and that even if they kill me I will not answer them to what they are asking me to do. After that, [the Imam] was transferred to Fadl b. Yaḥya al-Barmaki. He was imprisoned there for days, and Fadl b. Rabih used to send him a meal each night. He was the only one allowed to enter upon him, so [the Imam] did not eat and did not break his fast except on this meal which was sent to him. This condition remained for three days and nights. On the fourth night, a meal was presented to him by Fadl b. Yaḥya (not Fadl b. Rabih).

He (as) raised his hands to the sky and said: O Lord! You know that if I ate this before this day, I would have been performing suicide by my own hands. He ate, and then he got sick. The next day he was sent a doctor to inspect the illness. The doctor said to him: How are you? He did not answer him. When the doctor insisted, he let out the palm of his hand and showed it to the doctor and said: This is my disease. There was a greenness in his hand which indicated that he was poisoned, and the poison had gathered in that point. The doctor left and he said to: By Allah, he knows what you did to him more than you do! Then, he (as) passed away.
